$comment: Mateu <-> Figma design contract. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the design-to-code pipeline: the Figma plugin (design/figma/plugin) BUILDS the component library from this file; design/figma/to-yaml reads a Figma file (REST JSON) BACK through it and writes specs/ui YAML; modux's Figma importer maps instances to its own model for Java/C#/Python. Conventions: component names are 'Mateu/<Category>/<Name>'; 'variants' become Figma VARIANT axes (visual), 'props' are non-visual config written in the '#config' text layer (key=value; ...), 'texts' name the text layers whose content is a designer override that maps to the given param. 'yaml' is the YAML mapping (see yamlConventions.yaml); 'yamlNotDrawn' lists the YAML component types with no Figma counterpart, and why. 'sketch' is the compact draw spec the plugin renders (primitives: title, label, value, text, chip, fieldbox, hr, dot, bullets, bar, stepper, row, col, table, imagebox, button, tile, listrow, slot — a slot with a name is drawn as the frame 'slot:<name>').

yamlNotDrawn.AppData: Data, not a visual: a route's appData / a response.
yamlNotDrawn.ComponentRef: A reference to a named component of a `type: Components` file — written by hand.
yamlNotDrawn.CustomComponent: An app-registered component: no Mateu look to draw.
yamlNotDrawn.Element: A raw custom element (`name` + attributes): no Mateu look to draw.
yamlNotDrawn.EmbeddedView: Embeds a server-side view — a code concept.
yamlNotDrawn.MicroFrontend: An island of another Mateu app — composition, not a look.
yamlNotDrawn.Directory: Built from a menu (`menu: [Actionable]`), not drawn.
yamlNotDrawn.Partial: Drawn by convention: a frame named `partial:<ref>` (see yamlConventions).

yamlConventions.page: Every top-level frame of a page (Figma pages whose name starts with "Mateu ·" are the library and skipped; frames whose name starts with "_" are skipped) becomes one specs/ui file, named after the frame (slugified). A frame that is (or holds) an instance of a Mateu/Page Templates/<FormTemplate> component becomes a `type: Form` with that `template:`; any other frame is a FREE page (`type: Form`, its children = `content`). A top-level instance of Mateu/Shell/App becomes a `type: AppShell` file.
yamlConventions.slots: A slot is a frame named `slot:<name>`; its children fill it. Inside an instance (Figma slots, or a detached copy) or as a SIBLING of the page-template instance in the screen frame — siblings that are not slots go to `content`. The page toolbar is the `slot:toolbar` (Button instances, the primary first).
yamlConventions.texts: An entry's `texts` name the text layers read back; a layer whose content is still its own name (an unedited placeholder) is not read.
yamlConventions.config: The `#config` text layer holds `key=value; key2=value2` for the entry's `props`; empty values are not read.
yamlConventions.variants: An instance's VARIANT properties map to the params of the same name; a boolean `false` and a value listed in `yaml.defaults` are omitted.
yamlConventions.hidden: Hidden layers and layers whose name starts with "#" are never content.
yamlConventions.frames: A plain frame (not an instance) inside a page or slot is a layout: HorizontalLayout when its auto-layout is horizontal, else VerticalLayout — or the layout its name says (FormLayout, HorizontalLayout, VerticalLayout). A plain text layer is a Text (h2 from 24px, h3 from 18px).
yamlConventions.partial: A frame named `partial:<ref>` is a `{type: Partial, ref}` and its children are written once to partials/<ref>.yaml.
yamlConventions.yaml: Each entry's `yaml` says what it becomes: `type` (or `record` + `schema`: an object without a type, checked against that schema definition), `set` (constants at dotted paths), `params` (param -> dotted path, or {path, values, set, component+key, list+key, whenTrue}; null = drawn but not read), `items` (where `item.*` params collect, grouped by the layer's trailing number), `defaults` (values omitted), `slots` (slot -> {path, many | wrap, flatten}) and `into` (merged into the page, or appended to one of its lists). `yaml: null` = no YAML counterpart (see `yamlNote`).
